records.source: מַשָּׂ֖א בָּבֶ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן־אָמֽוֹץ׃
records.gloss: The oracle of Babylon which saw Isaiah son of Amoz.
pieces: The oracle about Babylon that Isaiah son of Amoz saw.

L.1: The oracle [concerning] Babylon, which Isaiah son of Amoz saw.

R.1: This is a message about Babylon. Isaiah son of Amoz received it in a vision.

decisions.choice: oracle: a solemn pronouncement from God, here a word of judgment on a nation
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "lift up". It can mean a load that is carried (a "burden") or a word that is lifted up, that is, pronounced. Here it is a pronouncement: in 2 Kings 9:25 the LORD "lifted up this oracle" against Ahab, and Jeremiah 23:33-38 plays on both senses. The word heads each of the oracles on the nations that follow in Isaiah 13-23 (14:28; 15:1; 17:1; 19:1; 21:1, 11, 13; 22:1; 23:1).

decisions.choice: Babylon: the great city on the Euphrates, and the empire that later ruled from it
decisions.reason: In Isaiah's day Assyria was the ruling power and Babylon was a subject city that often rebelled (39:1). Under Nebuchadnezzar it became the empire that destroyed Jerusalem in 587/586 BC, and it fell to Cyrus of Persia in 539 BC. The oracle stands first among the nations, and chapters 13-14 and 21:1-10 are given to it.

decisions.choice: saw: received in a vision
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for a prophet's vision (1:1; 2:1). What Isaiah "saw" was a word from God.

decisions.choice: a message ... received it in a vision
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the term "oracle" for each of the oracles on the nations; Readable says "message" throughout them. Readable also explains "saw" as receiving a vision.

records.heading: The oracle about Babylon

records.source: עַ֤ל הַר־נִשְׁפֶּה֙ שְֽׂאוּ־נֵ֔ס הָרִ֥ימוּ ק֖וֹל לָהֶ֑ם הָנִ֣יפוּ יָ֔ד וְיָבֹ֖אוּ פִּתְחֵ֥י נְדִיבִֽים׃
records.gloss: On a mountain swept bare lift up a standard, raise a voice to them, wave a hand, and let them go into [the] doors of nobles.
pieces: Hoist a signal flag on a bare hilltop; \q shout out to them; \q wave them on, \q so they march in through the gates of the nobles.

L.2: On a bare mountain lift up a signal flag; \q raise a voice to them; \q wave a hand, \q that they may go into the doors of nobles.

R.2: Raise a flag on a bare hilltop! \q Shout to the soldiers \q and wave them forward, \q so they can march in through the gates where the rulers live.

decisions.choice: a signal flag and a waving hand: signals that call an army together
decisions.reason: A pole with a banner set up on a high place, where no trees hide it, called troops to gather (5:26; 18:3; Jeremiah 51:27). Waving the hand beckoned them on. God is summoning an army, which verses 3-5 describe.

decisions.choice: the doors of nobles: the gates of the city of the great, the city to be attacked
alternatives: the gates of the nobles who send the army
decisions.reason: The army is to enter the gates of the rulers' city. The city is not named until verse 19, where it is Babylon.

decisions.choice: the soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable names "them" as the soldiers being called up, as verses 3-4 show.

records.source: אֲנִ֥י צִוֵּ֖יתִי לִמְקֻדָּשָׁ֑י גַּ֣ם קָרָ֤אתִי גִבּוֹרַי֙ לְאַפִּ֔י עַלִּיזֵ֖י גַּאֲוָתִֽי׃
records.gloss: I, I have commanded to my consecrated [ones]; also I have summoned my warriors for my anger, [the] exultant [ones] of my pride.
pieces: I myself have given orders to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} consecrated troops; \q I have called up {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} warriors to carry out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger, \q those who exult in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} majesty.

L.3: I have commanded {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} consecrated ones; \q I have also summoned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} warriors for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger, \q the exulting ones of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} majesty.

R.3: I have given orders to the soldiers I set apart for this. \q I have called {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} warriors to carry out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger. \q They rejoice in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} greatness.

decisions.choice: my consecrated ones: warriors set apart for a war God himself wages
decisions.reason: Soldiers were made holy before a battle fought at God's command (Joshua 3:5; 1 Samuel 21:6; Jeremiah 22:7; 51:27-28, "consecrate the nations" against Babylon). The armies that come are God's instruments, whoever they are.

decisions.choice: I: emphatic; God himself speaks
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out before the verb, which stresses it: it is God who gives the order. In this chapter God speaks in verses 3, 11-13 and 17-18, and the prophet in the rest.

decisions.choice: the exulting ones of my majesty: warriors who exult in God's majesty
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean those who rejoice in God's exaltation, or God's own proud and exultant warriors. Either way their triumph serves God's purpose. Zephaniah 3:11 uses the same words of proud people.

decisions.choice: the soldiers I set apart for this
decisions.reason: Readable explains "consecrated ones" as soldiers set apart for this war.

records.source: ק֥וֹל הָמ֛וֹן בֶּֽהָרִ֖ים דְּמ֣וּת עַם־רָ֑ב ק֠וֹל שְׁא֞וֹן מַמְלְכ֤וֹת גּוֹיִם֙ נֶֽאֱסָפִ֔ים יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת מְפַקֵּ֖ד צְבָ֥א מִלְחָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: [The] sound of a tumult on the mountains, [the] likeness of a people numerous; [the] sound of an uproar of kingdoms of nations gathering; Yahweh of hosts [is] mustering an army of battle.
pieces: Hear the roar on the mountains, like a vast multitude! \q Hear the din of kingdoms, of nations assembling! \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies is gathering an army for war.

L.4: [The] sound of a tumult on the mountains, like a great people! \q [The] sound of an uproar of kingdoms, of nations gathering! \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts is mustering an army for battle.

R.4: Listen to the noise on the mountains. It sounds like a huge crowd! \q Listen to the noise of kingdoms and nations coming together! \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies is getting an army ready for war.

decisions.choice: the sound of: an exclamation, "Listen!"
decisions.reason: The word "sound" stands at the head of a line with no verb, as a cry calling attention: "Hark!" (40:3, 6; 52:8).

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts is mustering an army: God himself is commander of the gathering troops
decisions.reason: The verb means to count and review troops before battle (Numbers 1:3; 2 Samuel 24:2). The title "LORD of hosts" (1:9) is fitting here: the many nations are his army.

decisions.choice: Hear ... Hear / Listen
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the exclamation a call to listen; Literal keeps "sound".

records.source: בָּאִ֛ים מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מֶרְחָ֖ק מִקְצֵ֣ה הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם יְהוָה֙ וּכְלֵ֣י זַעְמ֔וֹ לְחַבֵּ֖ל כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: [They are] coming from a land of distance, from [the] end of the heavens, Yahweh and the weapons of his indignation, to ruin all the earth.
pieces: They come from a faraway land, from the ends of the sky: \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the weapons of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fury, \q to ruin the whole earth.

L.5: [They are] coming from a distant land, from the end of the heavens, \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the weapons of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} indignation, \q to destroy all the earth.

R.5: They are coming from a land far away, from the farthest edge of the sky. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is coming with them. They are the weapons {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} uses in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger, \q and they will ruin the whole earth.

decisions.choice: the weapons of his indignation: the armies God uses to carry out his anger
decisions.reason: The nations are God's weapons, as Assyria was "the rod of my anger" in 10:5 and the same word for fury is used there. Jeremiah 50:25 says the same of Babylon's attackers.

decisions.choice: all the earth: the whole earth, with Babylon's land at its center
decisions.reason: The word can mean "land" or "earth". The chapter widens from Babylon to the whole world: verse 11 says "the world" and verse 13 sets "the earth" beside the heavens. The same word in verse 9 is read the same way.

decisions.choice: The LORD is coming with them. They are the weapons he uses
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the phrase into sentences and says plainly that the armies are the weapons.

records.source: הֵילִ֕ילוּ כִּ֥י קָר֖וֹב י֣וֹם יְהוָ֑ה כְּשֹׁ֖ד מִשַּׁדַּ֥י יָבֽוֹא׃
records.gloss: Wail, for near [is the] day of Yahweh; like devastation from [the] Almighty it will come.
pieces: Howl, for the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is close at hand! \q It will come like ruin from the Almighty.

L.6: Wail, for near [is] the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q Like destruction from [the] Almighty it will come.

R.6: Cry out in grief, for the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is near! \q It will come like ruin sent by God All-Powerful.

decisions.choice: the day of the LORD: the time when God acts in judgment
decisions.reason: The prophets speak of a coming day when God acts against all that is proud and wicked (2:12; Amos 5:18-20; Zephaniah 1:14-18). Here that day falls on Babylon, and in verses 9-13 on the whole world. The words of this verse are repeated in Joel 1:15.

decisions.choice: like destruction from the Almighty: a play on sound, shod and Shaddai
decisions.reason: "Destruction" (shod) and "the Almighty" (Shaddai) sound alike. The name Shaddai, used of God from Genesis 17:1, is traditionally taken to mean "the Almighty".

decisions.choice: Cry out in grief ... God All-Powerful
decisions.reason: Readable explains "wail" as a cry of grief and says "God All-Powerful" for the name Shaddai.

records.source: עַל־כֵּ֖ן כָּל־יָדַ֣יִם תִּרְפֶּ֑ינָה וְכָל־לְבַ֥ב אֱנ֖וֹשׁ יִמָּס׃
records.gloss: Therefore all hands will drop, and every heart of a mortal will melt.
pieces: So every hand will hang helpless, \q and the heart of every mortal will melt.

L.7: Therefore all hands will drop, \q and every heart of a mortal will melt.

R.7: So everyone's hands will hang weak, \q and everyone's courage will melt away.

decisions.choice: all hands will drop: people lose all strength to act
decisions.reason: Hands that hang down are a picture of helpless fear (Jeremiah 6:24; Ezekiel 7:17).

decisions.choice: every heart will melt: courage fails
decisions.reason: A melting heart is a picture of terror and lost courage (Joshua 2:11; 7:5; Ezekiel 21:12).

decisions.choice: everyone's courage will melt away
decisions.reason: Readable explains the melting heart as lost courage.

records.source: וְֽנִבְהָ֓לוּ׀צִירִ֤ים וַֽחֲבָלִים֙ יֹֽאחֵז֔וּן כַּיּוֹלֵדָ֖ה יְחִיל֑וּן אִ֤ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵ֨הוּ֙ יִתְמָ֔הוּ פְּנֵ֥י לְהָבִ֖ים פְּנֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And they will be terrified; pangs and labor-pains will seize [them]; like [one] who gives birth they will be in anguish; each to his neighbor they will look in astonishment; faces of flames [are] their faces.
pieces: They will be filled with dread; cramps and pains will take hold of them; \q they will writhe like a woman in labor. \q They will stare at one another in shock, \q their faces flushed like fire.

L.8: And they will be terrified; pangs and labor pains will seize [them]; \q like [a woman] giving birth they will writhe; \q each will look in astonishment at his neighbor; \q faces of flames [will be] their faces.

R.8: People will be terrified. Pain will grab them like the pain of a woman having a baby. \q They will stare at each other in shock, \q and their faces will turn red as fire.

decisions.choice: like a woman giving birth: sudden, gripping pain that cannot be escaped
decisions.reason: Labor pains are a common picture of anguish in the face of disaster (21:3; 26:17; Jeremiah 6:24; 50:43, of the king of Babylon).

decisions.choice: faces of flames: faces burning red with fear and shame
decisions.reason: The phrase is short and its exact sense is uncertain. It most likely describes faces flushed with terror or shame; some take it as faces lit by the flames of the burning city.

decisions.choice: People
decisions.reason: Readable supplies the subject: the people struck by the day of the LORD.

records.source: הִנֵּ֤ה יוֹם־יְהוָה֙ בָּ֔א אַכְזָרִ֥י וְעֶבְרָ֖ה וַחֲר֣וֹן אָ֑ף לָשׂ֤וּם הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה וְחַטָּאֶ֖יהָ יַשְׁמִ֥יד מִמֶּֽנָּה׃
records.gloss: There! [The] day of Yahweh [is] coming, cruel, and wrath and burning of anger, to make the earth into a waste; and its sinners he will destroy from it.
pieces: Look, the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is on its way, \q merciless, full of fury and blazing anger, \q to turn the earth into a wasteland; \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will wipe out the sinners who live in it.

L.9: Look, the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is coming, \q cruel, [with] fury and burning anger, \q to make the earth a desolation; \q and its sinners {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will destroy from it.

R.9: Look! The day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is coming. \q It will be a cruel day, full of terrible anger. \q It will turn the earth into an empty wasteland, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will destroy the sinners who live there.

decisions.choice: cruel: without mercy
decisions.reason: The word describes what is pitiless and fierce (Jeremiah 6:23; 50:42, of the army that comes against Babylon). The day itself shows no mercy to the proud.

decisions.choice: he will destroy: the LORD is the subject
decisions.reason: The verb is masculine singular. It may continue with the day as subject ("it will destroy"), but in verses 11-13 God himself acts, so it is read of him.

decisions.choice: its sinners: judgment falls on the wicked
decisions.reason: The day of the LORD is aimed at sinners, the proud and the ruthless of verse 11, not at the earth for its own sake (compare 2:11-17).

records.source: כִּֽי־כוֹכְבֵ֤י הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ וּכְסִ֣ילֵיהֶ֔ם לֹ֥א יָהֵ֖לּוּ אוֹרָ֑ם חָשַׁ֤ךְ הַשֶּׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ בְּצֵאת֔וֹ וְיָרֵ֖חַ לֹֽא־יַגִּ֥יהַ אוֹרֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: For the stars of the heavens and their constellations will not flash forth their light; it will be dark, the sun, when it goes forth, and [the] moon will not make shine its light.
pieces: The stars of the sky and their constellations will not send out their light; \q the sun will be darkened as it comes up, \q and the moon will not let its light shine.

L.10: For the stars of the heavens and their constellations will not flash forth their light; \q the sun will be dark at its going out, \q and [the] moon will not make its light shine.

R.10: The stars and the star patterns in the sky will not shine. \q The sun will be dark when it rises, \q and the moon will give no light.

decisions.choice: their constellations: literally "their Orions"
decisions.reason: The word is the name of the constellation Orion (Amos 5:8; Job 9:9; 38:31), used in the plural for the great star groups of the sky.

decisions.choice: darkened sun, moon and stars: a sign of the day of the LORD
decisions.reason: The prophets describe God's day of judgment with the lights of the sky going dark (Joel 2:10; 4:15; Ezekiel 32:7-8; Amos 8:9). Jesus uses this verse in Matthew 24:29 and Mark 13:24.

decisions.choice: the star patterns
decisions.reason: Readable explains "constellations" in plain words.

records.source: וּפָקַדְתִּ֤י עַל־תֵּבֵל֙ רָעָ֔ה וְעַל־רְשָׁעִ֖ים עֲוֺנָ֑ם וְהִשְׁבַּתִּי֙ גְּא֣וֹן זֵדִ֔ים וְגַאֲוַ֥ת עָרִיצִ֖ים אַשְׁפִּֽיל׃
records.gloss: And I will visit on [the] world evil, and on wicked [people] their iniquity; and I will put an end to [the] pride of arrogant [people], and [the] haughtiness of ruthless [people] I will bring low.
pieces: I will call the world to account for its evil \q and the wicked for their guilt. \q I will end the pride of the arrogant \q and bring down the haughtiness of tyrants.

L.11: And I will visit upon [the] world [its] evil, \q and upon [the] wicked their iniquity; \q and I will put an end to the pride of the arrogant, \q and the haughtiness of the ruthless I will bring low.

R.11: I will punish the world for the evil it has done \q and punish wicked people for their sins. \q I will stop proud people from boasting, \q and I will humble cruel people who think they are great.

decisions.choice: I will visit: I will call to account and punish
decisions.reason: The verb means to attend to or inspect. With "upon" and a wrong done, it means God deals with the wrong by punishing it (10:12; 24:21; 26:21).

decisions.choice: the world: the whole inhabited earth
decisions.reason: This word always means the inhabited world, never a single country (14:17, 21; 24:4). It shows that the judgment reaches beyond Babylon.

decisions.choice: pride ... haughtiness ... I will bring low: the theme of 2:11-17
decisions.reason: Isaiah repeats that on the day of the LORD all human pride will be brought low and the LORD alone will be exalted (2:11, 17; 5:15).

records.source: אוֹקִ֥יר אֱנ֖וֹשׁ מִפָּ֑ז וְאָדָ֖ם מִכֶּ֥תֶם אוֹפִֽיר׃
records.gloss: I will make rare a mortal more than pure gold, and a human more than the gold of Ophir.
pieces: I will make human beings harder to find than refined gold, \q and mortals scarcer than gold from Ophir.

L.12: I will make mortals more rare than fine gold, \q and humankind than [the] gold of Ophir.

R.12: So few people will be left alive that they will be harder to find than pure gold, \q even the fine gold from Ophir.

decisions.choice: I will make rare: so few survive that people become scarce
decisions.reason: The verb means to make precious or rare (1 Samuel 3:1, "the word of the LORD was rare"). The judgment will leave only a few alive (compare 6:11-13; 24:6).

decisions.choice: Ophir: a distant land famous for its fine gold
decisions.reason: Solomon's ships brought gold from Ophir (1 Kings 9:28; 10:11). Where it lay is not known.

decisions.choice: So few people will be left alive
decisions.reason: Readable explains the comparison: people will be rare because few survive.

records.source: עַל־כֵּן֙ שָׁמַ֣יִם אַרְגִּ֔יז וְתִרְעַ֥שׁ הָאָ֖רֶץ מִמְּקוֹמָ֑הּ בְּעֶבְרַת֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וּבְי֖וֹם חֲר֥וֹן אַפּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Therefore [the] heavens I will make tremble, and will shake the earth from its place, in the wrath of Yahweh of hosts and in [the] day of the burning of his anger.
pieces: So I will make the sky shudder, \q and the earth will be jolted out of its place \q by the fury of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q on the day {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger blazes.

L.13: Therefore I will make [the] heavens tremble, \q and the earth will shake from its place, \q at the fury of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, \q and in [the] day of the burning of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger.

R.13: So I will shake the sky, \q and the earth will be knocked out of its place. \q This will happen because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies is furious, \q on the day {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger burns hot.

decisions.choice: I ... the LORD of hosts: God speaks of himself by name
decisions.reason: God speaks in the first person ("I will make tremble") and then names himself in the third person. The prophets often move this way between God's words and words about him (compare 1:24).

decisions.choice: heavens tremble, earth shakes: the whole created order shaken
decisions.reason: Heaven and earth shaking mark God's coming in judgment (2:19, 21; 24:18-20; Joel 2:10; 4:16; Haggai 2:6).

records.source: וְהָיָה֙ כִּצְבִ֣י מֻדָּ֔ח וּכְצֹ֖אן וְאֵ֣ין מְקַבֵּ֑ץ אִ֤ישׁ אֶל־עַמּוֹ֙ יִפְנ֔וּ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶל־אַרְצ֖וֹ יָנֽוּסוּ׃
records.gloss: And it will be, like a gazelle hunted and like sheep, and there [will] not [be one who] gathers, each to his people they will turn, and each to his land they will flee.
pieces: Like a gazelle being chased, \q like sheep that no one rounds up, \q they will each turn back to their own people and run off, \q each one to their own country.

L.14: And it will be, like a hunted gazelle, \q and like sheep with none gathering [them], \q each to his people they will turn, \q and each to his land they will flee.

R.14: People will scatter like a hunted gazelle, \q like sheep with no shepherd to gather them. \q Each one will hurry back to their own people \q and run home to their own land.

decisions.choice: each to his people, each to his land: foreigners in Babylon flee home
decisions.reason: Babylon was full of traders, soldiers and captives from many nations. When the city falls they will scatter to their homelands. Jeremiah uses the same words about Babylon's fall (Jeremiah 50:16; 51:9).

decisions.choice: gazelle: a swift, timid animal fleeing a hunter
decisions.reason: The same word means "beauty" in verse 19, where Babylon is "the beauty of kingdoms". The proud city's people become a hunted animal.

decisions.choice: People will scatter ... with no shepherd
decisions.reason: Readable supplies the subject and explains "no one gathers" as having no shepherd.

records.source: כָּל־הַנִּמְצָ֖א יִדָּקֵ֑ר וְכָל־הַנִּסְפֶּ֖ה יִפּ֥וֹל בֶּחָֽרֶב׃
records.gloss: Every [one who] is found will be pierced through, and every [one who] is captured will fall by [the] sword.
pieces: Anyone who is found will be run through, \q and anyone who is seized will be cut down by the sword.

L.15: Everyone who is found will be pierced through, \q and everyone who is caught will fall by the sword.

R.15: Anyone the enemy finds will be stabbed. \q Anyone they catch will be killed with the sword.

decisions.choice: who is caught: taken, swept up
decisions.reason: The verb may mean "swept away" or "added", and here most likely those caught as they flee. Whether people hide or run, none escape (compare 24:18).

decisions.choice: everyone ... everyone: no one escapes
decisions.reason: The two matching lines say the same thing twice for emphasis.

decisions.choice: the enemy
decisions.reason: Readable names who finds them: the attacking army.

records.source: וְעֹלְלֵיהֶ֥ם יְרֻטְּשׁ֖וּ לְעֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם יִשַּׁ֨סּוּ֙ בָּֽתֵּיהֶ֔ם וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם תִּשָּׁכַֽבְנָה׃
records.gloss: And their infants will be dashed in pieces before their eyes; their houses will be plundered, and their wives will be lain with.
pieces: Before their eyes their little children will be smashed; \q their houses will be looted \q and their wives raped.

L.16: And their infants will be dashed in pieces before their eyes; \q their houses will be plundered, \q and their wives will be lain with.

R.16: Their babies will be killed in front of them. \q Their houses will be robbed, \q and their wives will be raped.

decisions.choice: will be lain with: the qere; the written text has "will be violated"
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text mean "will be ravished". The scribes' marginal reading, used in public reading, puts a milder word, "lain with", in its place, as they do in Deuteronomy 28:30 and Zechariah 14:2. Both describe rape.

decisions.choice: infants dashed in pieces: the brutal practice of ancient conquest
decisions.reason: Conquering armies killed children so that no one would survive to fight again (2 Kings 8:12; Hosea 14:1; Nahum 3:10). The verse describes the horror that falls on Babylon; it does not approve it. Psalm 137:8-9 speaks of the same fate for Babylon.

records.source: הִנְנִ֛י מֵעִ֥יר עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם אֶת־מָדָ֑י אֲשֶׁר־כֶּ֨סֶף֙ לֹ֣א יַחְשֹׁ֔בוּ וְזָהָ֖ב לֹ֥א יַחְפְּצוּ־בֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Here I [am] about to rouse against them the Media, who silver not they value, and gold not they delight in it.
pieces: Look, I am rousing the Medes to attack them, \q a people who count silver as nothing \q and care nothing for gold.

L.17: Look, I am stirring up against them the Medes, \q who do not value silver, \q and [in] gold they do not delight.

R.17: Look! I am going to make the Medes attack them. \q The Medes cannot be paid off with silver or gold.

decisions.choice: the Medes: a people of the mountains of western Iran
decisions.reason: The Medes joined Babylon to destroy Nineveh, the capital of Assyria, in 612 BC. Later they were united with the Persians under Cyrus, whose armies took Babylon in 539 BC. Jeremiah 51:11, 28 and Daniel 5:28 also name the Medes as Babylon's conquerors. Isaiah 21:2 names Media with Elam.

decisions.choice: they do not value silver: they cannot be bought off
decisions.reason: A city under attack might pay tribute to make an army go away (2 Kings 18:14). The Medes want conquest, not payment, so no ransom will save Babylon.

decisions.choice: I am stirring up: God rouses the nations to act
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of God raising Cyrus in 41:2, 25 and 45:13, and of stirring up the Medes against Babylon in Jeremiah 51:1, 11. The armies act by their own choice, yet God directs them.

decisions.choice: cannot be paid off with silver or gold
decisions.reason: Readable explains what it means that they do not value silver and gold.

records.source: וּקְשָׁת֖וֹת נְעָרִ֣ים תְּרַטַּ֑שְׁנָה וּפְרִי־בֶ֨טֶן֙ לֹ֣א יְרַחֵ֔מוּ עַל־בָּנִ֖ים לֹֽא־תָח֥וּס עֵינָֽם׃
records.gloss: And bows youths will dash in pieces; and [the] fruit of [the] womb not they will have compassion on; on children not will look with pity their eye.
pieces: Their bows will strike down the young men; \q they will show no mercy to newborn babies, \q and they will look on children without pity.

L.18: And [their] bows will dash young men in pieces; \q and [the] fruit of [the] womb they will not pity; \q on children their eye will not look with compassion.

R.18: Their archers will shoot down the young men. \q They will not show mercy even to babies or feel sorry for children.

decisions.choice: bows will dash young men in pieces: archers will cut down the young men
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for infants in verse 16, and it fits bows oddly. The bow stands for the archer: the Medes were known as archers (Jeremiah 50:9, 14, 29; 51:3).

decisions.choice: the fruit of the womb: babies, children newly born
decisions.reason: The phrase means a mother's offspring (Genesis 30:2; Deuteronomy 7:13).

decisions.choice: their eye will not pity: they will feel no compassion
decisions.reason: Mercy is said to be in the eye, which sees and spares (Deuteronomy 7:16; Ezekiel 7:4).

decisions.choice: archers
decisions.reason: Readable says "archers" for "bows".

records.source: וְהָיְתָ֤ה בָבֶל֙ צְבִ֣י מַמְלָכ֔וֹת תִּפְאֶ֖רֶת גְּא֣וֹן כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֣ת אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶת־סְדֹ֖ם וְאֶת־עֲמֹרָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it will be, Babylon, [the] beauty of kingdoms, the splendor of the pride of [the] Chaldeans, like the overthrow of God [of] Sodom and Gomorrah.
pieces: Babylon, the gem among kingdoms, \q the splendor the Chaldeans are so proud of, \q will become what Sodom and Gomorrah became when God overturned them.

L.19: And Babylon, [the] beauty of kingdoms, \q the splendor of the pride of [the] Chaldeans, \q will be like God's overthrowing of Sodom and Gomorrah.

R.19: Babylon is the most beautiful of all kingdoms. \q It is the pride and glory of the Chaldean people. \q But God will destroy it, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} destroyed the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah.

decisions.choice: the Chaldeans: the people of southern Babylonia
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans were tribes of the marshlands in the south of Babylonia. Merodach-baladan (39:1) was a Chaldean, and so was the dynasty of Nebuchadnezzar. The name came to stand for the Babylonians (Daniel 5:30).

decisions.choice: the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah: total destruction sent by God
decisions.reason: Genesis 19:25 uses the same verb, "overthrow". The cities' fate became the standard picture of complete ruin (1:9; Deuteronomy 29:22; Amos 4:11), and Jeremiah 50:40 applies it to Babylon.

decisions.choice: beauty: the same word as "gazelle" in verse 14
decisions.reason: The word means beauty or glory (4:2; 28:1) and is also the name of the gazelle. The jewel of kingdoms ends like a hunted animal.

decisions.choice: But God will destroy it, as he destroyed the cities
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the verse into sentences and says plainly what the overthrow is.

records.source: לֹֽא־תֵשֵׁ֣ב לָנֶ֔צַח וְלֹ֥א תִשְׁכֹּ֖ן עַד־דּ֣וֹר וָד֑וֹר וְלֹֽא־יַהֵ֥ל שָׁם֙ עֲרָבִ֔י וְרֹעִ֖ים לֹא־יַרְבִּ֥צוּ שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: Not it will remain to perpetuity, and not it will settle until generation and generation; and not will pitch tent there an Arab, and shepherds not will make lie down there.
pieces: No one will ever live there again or settle there, from one generation to the next. \q No Arab will set up a tent there, \q and no shepherds will bed down their flocks there.

L.20: It will never be inhabited, \q and it will not be dwelt in to generation and generation; \q and an Arab will not pitch [a tent] there, \q and shepherds will not make [their flocks] lie down there.

R.20: No one will ever live there again, not in any generation. \q Not even desert nomads will camp there, \q and shepherds will not let their sheep rest there.

decisions.choice: it will not remain ... it will not settle: the city will not be lived in
decisions.reason: The verbs "sit" and "dwell" have the city as their subject: it will not be inhabited (Jeremiah 50:13, 39; Zechariah 12:6).

decisions.choice: an Arab ... shepherds: nomads who camp anywhere
decisions.reason: Wandering herders of the desert pitched their tents wherever they found grazing. Even they will avoid the ruins.

decisions.choice: desert nomads
decisions.reason: Readable explains "Arab" as the wandering herders of the desert.

records.source: וְרָבְצוּ־שָׁ֣ם צִיִּ֔ים וּמָלְא֥וּ בָתֵּיהֶ֖ם אֹחִ֑ים וְשָׁ֤כְנוּ שָׁם֙ בְּנ֣וֹת יַֽעֲנָ֔ה וּשְׂעִירִ֖ים יְרַקְּדוּ־שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And will lie down there desert-dwellers, and will be full their houses [of] howling creatures, and will dwell there daughters of [the] ostrich, and goats will leap about there.
pieces: Desert beasts will make their dens there instead; \q screeching creatures will crowd the houses. \q Ostriches will settle there, \q and wild goats will prance there.

L.21: And desert creatures will lie down there, \q and their houses will be full of howling creatures; \q and ostriches will dwell there, \q and goats will leap about there.

R.21: Instead, wild animals of the desert will rest there, \q and the houses will be full of howling animals. \q Ostriches will live there, \q and wild goats will jump around there.

decisions.choice: desert creatures, howling creatures: wild animals of waste places
decisions.reason: These are animals of the desert and of ruins (34:14; Jeremiah 50:39). Which kinds are meant is not certain; the second word may name jackals or owls.

decisions.choice: daughters of the ostrich: ostriches
decisions.reason: The phrase is a usual way of naming the ostrich (34:13; Job 30:29). Some take it as the eagle owl.

decisions.choice: goats: wild goats
decisions.reason: The word means "hairy ones", goats. In Leviticus 17:7 the same word names goat-idols or demons, and some read it that way here and in 34:14.

records.source: וְעָנָ֤ה אִיִּים֙ בְּאַלְמנוֹתָ֔יווְתַנִּ֖ים בְּהֵ֣יכְלֵי עֹ֑נֶג וְקָר֤וֹב לָבוֹא֙ עִתָּ֔הּ וְיָמֶ֖יהָ לֹ֥א יִמָּשֵֽׁכוּ׃
records.gloss: And will sing hyenas in its palaces, and jackals in [the] palaces of delight; and near to come [is] its time, and its days not will be prolonged.
pieces: Hyenas will call to one another in its fortresses, \q and jackals in its luxurious palaces. \q Its hour has nearly come; \q its days will not be drawn out.

L.22: And hyenas will cry in its fortresses, \q and jackals in [the] palaces of delight; \q and near to come [is] its time, \q and its days will not be prolonged.

R.22: Hyenas will howl in its forts, \q and jackals in its fine palaces. \q The time for Babylon to fall is almost here. \q Its days will soon be over.

decisions.choice: its fortresses: the word read as a form of the word for fortress
decisions.reason: As written, the word looks like "its widows". It is read as a spelling of the word for fortresses or palaces, with l for r, which matches "palaces" in the next line (compare 34:13).

decisions.choice: hyenas will cry ... jackals: wild animals calling in the ruins
decisions.reason: The verb means to sing or answer; here the animals call to one another. The names of the animals are not certain (34:13-14).

decisions.choice: its time is near: the judgment will not be delayed
decisions.reason: Though Babylon's fall lay many years ahead of Isaiah, God's word presents it as close and certain.

decisions.choice: The time for Babylon to fall
decisions.reason: Readable names Babylon and says what "its time" means.
